record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group that is non-trivial, separable, and metrizable?

evidence.quote: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group which is a non-trivial separable metrizable topological group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a topological group (i.e., a group equipped with a topology making multiplication and inversion continuous). A topological space is said to be totally disconnected if its only connected subsets are singletons. A topological space is separable if it has a countable dense subset, and metrizable if its topology is induced by some metric. A quotient group of $G$ is the group $G/N$ for some closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$, endowed with the quotient topology.

Question: Is it true that for every topological group $G$ which is not totally disconnected, there exists a closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ such that the quotient topological group $G/N$ is non-trivial, separable, and metrizable?
artifact.status_search_result: Leiderman, Morris, and Tkachenko (2017/2019, "The Separable Quotient Problem for Topological Groups", Israel J. Math.) explicitly considered the four analogues of asking whether every non-totally disconnected topological group admits a separable quotient that is (i) non-trivial, (ii) infinite, (iii) metrizable, or (iv) infinite metrizable, and answered all four in the negative. In particular, they construct an uncountable precompact group having no non-trivial separable quotient, which also refutes the version with the additional metrizability requirement. Positive results hold for compact groups, (σ-compact) locally compact (abelian) groups, abelian/σ-compact pro-Lie groups, and pseudocompact groups.

status_evidence.title: The Separable Quotient Problem for Topological Groups (arXiv:1707.09546)
status_evidence.snippet: There are four natural analogues for non-totally disconnected topological groups: whether every such group has a separable quotient group which is (i) non-trivial; (ii) infinite; (iii) metrizable; (iv) infinite metrizable. All four questions are answered here in the negative.
status_evidence.claim: The question is answered negatively: there exist non-totally disconnected topological groups with no non-trivial separable (metrizable) quotient.

status_evidence.title: The separable quotient problem for topological groups, Israel Journal of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of Leiderman–Morris–Tkachenko establishing the negative answers and the precompact counterexample.
status_evidence.claim: Published peer-reviewed confirmation that all four analogues are answered in the negative, with positive results for several special classes.
